description: Core AI agent detection engine for .NET. Detects AI agents (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, etc.) via user-agent patterns, header analysis, and behavioral signals. Platform-agnostic — use with any .NET HTTP server, including ASP.NET Core (via Checkpoint.AspNetCore) and classic .NET Framework 4.6.2+ (via Checkpoint.AspNet).
releaseNotes:
1.15.0

Breaking changes:
- Removed: The public resolution types `DidWebResolver`, `DidWebLocation`, `EngineDidDocument`, `EngineVerificationMethod`, `IssuerAllowlist`, `JsonWebKey2020Validator`, `SsrfSafeDidFetcher`, `DidFetchResponse`, `StatusIssuerDocuments`, `StatusListRegistry`, `StatusListResolver`, `StatusListResult`, `TtlCache<T>` and `DelegationDidDocs`, the `IResolutionWarmer` members `TryGetDidDoc`, `TryGetStatus` and `RegisterStatus`, and the public `ResolutionWarmer` constructor.
  The engine decodes documents itself now; use `ResolutionWarmer.CreateDefault`.
  The published adapters (1.11.9 and 1.14.0) call only `CreateDefault`, `PrimeAsync` and `RefreshTickAsync`, which stay. (#6607)
- Removed: `AuthorizeInputProjection.IsUnverifiedOptimisticProtocolBlock` and `VerificationMethod.McpIHandshake`.
  The engine refuses MCP-I and never reports a handshake, so neither was ever reached; `mcp_i_handshake` and `kyaos_handshake` are no longer treated as a verified identity by a composed policy or the dashboard allow list. (#6642)

Added:
- Engine-directed resolution: the SDK fetches the DID documents and status lists the engine names for a presented credential, in the background, from public HTTPS hosts only, and answers each request from its cache.
  A resource not fetched yet is answered 503 `kyaos/identity-pending` or `kyaos/status-pending`; a resource whose fetch failed is decided by the engine (for example `kyaos/did-unresolvable` for a signer's 404), where it used to stay pending.
  Servers need outbound HTTPS to the trusted roots and to the `did:web` hosts of the agents and issuers they accept. (#6607)
- `DelegationHolder.CustomerId`: the id after `:users:` in `Subject`, set only when the credential's issuer
  (the root that signed it) is one of the configured `TrustedDelegationRoots` and `Subject` is exactly
  `<issuer>:users:<id>`, with one non-empty segment after it. It is null for anything else: a `did:key`, another
  host's or organization's DID (including a user under a different trusted root than the signer), extra segments, or
  no trusted roots. A merchant acting as the shopper on a delegated request reads it instead of parsing `Subject`. It
  is the merchant's own customer id when the shopper signed in on Checkpoint's consent page with the merchant's
  sign-in (merchant OAuth, credential or token); with Checkpoint's sign-in methods it is an id Checkpoint assigned. (#6367)

Changed:
- An engine Block is answered as the engine renders it: the kya-os/http registry status for a `kyaos/*` code (for example 401 for `kyaos/missing-signature` and `kyaos/did-unresolvable`, 429 with `Retry-After: 1` for `kyaos/replay-capacity`), the reason-keyed status otherwise, and the engine's JSON body and `X-Checkpoint-*` headers, in either response format and in both adapters.
  Engine policy blocks now return the engine's status and body, not the configured notice.
  `BlockedResponse` and the PlainText notice apply only to blocks the SDK decides: the configured `OnAgentDetected` action, the structured dashboard policy, browser posture, and `kyaos/policy-unavailable`, `kyaos/verification-pending` and `kyaos/application-authorization-unavailable`. (#6590)
- `kyaos/identity-pending` and `kyaos/status-pending` answer with `Retry-After: 1` (was 3). (#6607)
- A status list must be hosted on its issuer's `did:web` host; a list on another trusted root's host no longer counts. (#6607)
- A delegation signed by an issuer key listed without assertion authority is refused as 401 `kyaos/did-unresolvable` (it was 403 `kyaos/chain-broken`), like an unlisted key. (#6607)
- DID documents are refreshed on the engine's maximum age (every 150 seconds for 300) instead of every 55 minutes, and a source that keeps failing is retried at most once per 30 seconds. (#6607)
- The embedded engines carry a refreshed OpenAI signing-key record (the same key, valid for longer). (#6652)

Deprecated:
- `CheckpointOptions.StatusListWarmTargets` is no longer used; a set value is logged once at startup. (#6607)

Fixed:
- The embedded engine, in engine-directed resolution, uses only the keys a DID document authorises for each purpose. Not used by the host yet. (#6576)
- A delegation credential whose status-list index is outside the list is refused (`kyaos/chain-broken`). (#6609)
- A kya-http/2 request signed by a `did:web` key that is not a trusted root now verifies; it was always `kyaos/did-unresolvable`. (#6607)
- ASP.NET Core: if adding the discovery `Link` header throws, the middleware logs a warning and sends the
  response without that header. The header is added when the response starts, so the exception used to fail the
  application's whole response. (#6386)
- One 5-second deadline bounds each DID document and status list fetch from the connect to the last body byte, TLS handshake included, so a slow peer cannot hold a fetch past it. (#6674)
- a Web Bot Auth request verified against OpenAI's key directory is named `ChatGPT`, as Tier 3 names the same agent, instead of `openai`, so a policy that names ChatGPT matches it verified or not. `openai` stays in `metadata.verified_vendor` and `detected_agent.vendor`. (#6652)

Other merged changes:
- chore(rules): refresh AI vendor IPs 2026-10-21 (#6506)

Already shipped in an earlier release: #6483.
